title: Drop fork entirely; two vehicles only, with cross-surface parity enforced by roster composition
context: SPEC revision 2 treats the fork subagent type as a first-class routing vehicle (section 2 conflict C4, one load-bearing sentence in section 5.3), and records its absence in the desktop app as an accepted risk in section 10.4. The user works in both the CLI and the desktop app and requires identical configuration behaviour on both.U+000AU+000AA direct probe on 2026-09-11 established that section 2.1's framing is wrong in mechanism. Fork is not entrypoint-derived: the binary carries isForkSubagentEnabled and tengu_fork_subagent_enabled, the internal feature-gate namespace, so availability is a server-side flag. A desktop dispatch fails hard with "Agent type 'fork' not found". No env var, settings key or local statsig cache exposes or overrides it, in either direction. The flag can move with no release and no config change.U+000AU+000AThat makes any routing rule naming fork a prose claim about a flag nobody here can read or set - the exact class of cached capability statement the SPEC's own section 5.4 prohibits. The SPEC condemns its own section 5.3 sentence.
options: A. Two vehicles only - main and cold subagent. Fork is never named in any configuration file. Parity is structural (class S): the config cannot express a surface-dependent route.

B. SPEC as written - fork where available, main as fallback. Parity is advisory only: the same config yields materially different main-thread context occupancy per surface, and drifts further when the gate moves.
C. Runtime self-test on fork availability, branching on the result. Parity is advisory, and it adds the class-A routing layer that SPEC section 11 explicitly refuses to add.
outcome: Option A, selected by the user. Fork is removed from the SPEC; the configuration names two vehicles, main and cold subagent.U+000AU+000AWhy A over B and C: parity becomes a property of what the configuration can express rather than a behaviour asked of the model, and the config stops depending on a flag that cannot be read or set from here. B leaves the two surfaces genuinely divergent and degrades silently when the gate moves. C is the advisory routing layer section 11 rejects.U+000AU+000AThe cost is real and accepted: section 1.3 names main-thread context occupancy as the remediation's primary objective, and fork was the only vehicle reducing it without a re-typed brief. On CLI, step-dependent high-volume work now floods main, with harness summarization as the fallback - a fidelity loss, not a failure. Recorded as a spine risk in the same turn.U+000AU+000AThe cost is bounded because volume and step-dependency rarely co-occur once reads and writes are routed out. Explore takes a question and keeps many-file reads out of main; machinist takes a file list and keeps many-file writes out. What remains in main is reasoning, which is low-volume. The residual is step-dependent discovery such as debugging, whose mitigation is the ledger surviving compaction plus systematic-debugging as an on-demand skill.U+000AU+000AConcrete edits: section 5.3's final paragraph replaces the fork sentence with "Everything a dispatched agent needs must be addressable without this conversation: a path, a commit range, or a question. Work that can only be described by referring to what has already happened here is work that stays here." Sections 2.1 and 10.4 become recorded environment facts rather than routing inputs. Section 3.2 keeps fork only as the contrast justifying machinist, which holds whether or not fork is reachable.U+000AU+000AThis narrows the consequence drawn from conflict C4 - that fork is central to the spec - while leaving intact the precedence rule that documentation outranks the course material, which decision 01M2971A2T89BD9H0J0Y937TBD settled. It therefore supersedes nothing.U+000AU+000ASubagent best practice is satisfied structurally, not by prose. Every retained agent's entire input is addressable from outside the conversation: a diff for the two reviewers, two resolvable paths for conformance-auditor, a question for researcher, an enumerated file list for machinist. The three agents whose work was inherently step-dependent - delivery-lead, architect, investigator - are deleted, and their work returns to main. There is no agent left to dispatch step-dependent work to. Machinist's entry invariant is equivalent to context-independence rather than a proxy for it: if the change had needed discovery its files could not have been enumerated in advance.U+000AU+000ATwo amendments proposed to the user, not yet decided, and not folded in: (1) extend the reviewers' entry invariant to require that any standard the diff is reviewed against resolves to a path, mirroring conformance-auditor, which closes the case of a reviewer briefed with conversational criteria; (2) add a section 8 check that grep -rniE '\bfork\b' over rules, agents and CLAUDE.md returns 0, so the removal is structural rather than advisory.
